title: How to Scan Receipts Into QuickBooks Online Automatically
meta_description: Learn how to scan receipts into QuickBooks Online automatically via the app, email forwarding and bulk upload, then fix misreads in 10 minutes a week.
quick_answer: To scan receipts into QuickBooks Online automatically, connect your bank feeds, then capture receipts three ways: snap paper receipts in the QuickBooks mobile app, forward email receipts to your company's receipt forwarding address, or bulk-upload files in the Receipts tab. QuickBooks reads the vendor, date and amount, suggests a category and matching bank transaction, and you confirm. A short weekly review catches misreads. Features vary by plan and region.
key_takeaways: Use all three built-in capture routes: the mobile app for paper, your forwarding address for email receipts, and bulk upload in the Receipts tab for backlogs.
Connect every bank and card feed first. QuickBooks can only suggest a match for a transaction it has already downloaded.
Choose Match instead of Create expense whenever the bank charge already exists. Otherwise the same cost gets recorded twice.
Check faded, foreign-currency, tipped and split receipts by eye every time, because that's where the automatic reading most often goes wrong.
Set aside 10 minutes a week to clear the For review list, chase missing receipts and delete duplicates.
Check which features your plan and region include on Intuit's site. Check your tax authority's record-keeping rules before you throw away paper receipts.
who_this_is_for: This guide is for small-business owners, freelancers and bookkeepers who use QuickBooks Online and want receipts captured, read and matched to bank transactions with as little typing as possible.
intro: Most people mean to deal with receipts later, and later often means a shoebox at tax time. QuickBooks Online can take much of that work off your hands. It reads a photo or PDF of a receipt, pulls out the vendor, date and amount, and suggests which bank transaction the receipt belongs to. This guide covers each built-in capture method and the settings that help matching work. It also shows where the automatic reading goes wrong, gives you a 10-minute weekly review, and adds an optional Zapier step for Gmail. Intuit changes menus and features over time, so check the details below against your own account and plan.

steps.name: Confirm the features in your plan and region
steps.text: Open Intuit's plan comparison and help pages for your country. Confirm that your QuickBooks Online plan includes receipt capture, email forwarding and bank feeds, and note any limits on file types or sizes.

steps.name: Connect every bank and card account
steps.text: Link every account you pay business expenses from, including secondary cards. QuickBooks needs downloaded transactions before it can suggest a match, so fix any feed that shows a connection error.

steps.name: Install the mobile app and snap a test receipt
steps.text: Sign in to the QuickBooks mobile app, open the + or New menu and choose the receipt option, which is often called Receipt snap. Photograph one receipt and check that it appears in the Receipts tab on the web.

steps.name: Set up your receipt forwarding address
steps.text: In the Receipts tab on the web, choose the option to forward receipts from email. Copy your company's unique address, add every email address that is allowed to send to it, and forward one test receipt.

steps.name: Bulk upload your backlog
steps.text: On a computer, open the Receipts tab and drag in your scanned receipts, or select several files to upload. Save one receipt per file so each one is read separately.

steps.name: Review and confirm each receipt
steps.text: Open the For review list and check the payee, date, amount, category and payment account on each receipt. Choose Match when the bank transaction already exists. Use Create expense only for cash purchases or accounts that aren't connected.

steps.name: Add bank rules for regular vendors
steps.text: For subscriptions and suppliers you pay often, create rules in the bank transactions area so those charges are always categorised the same way. Test a new rule on a few transactions before you let it add anything automatically.

steps.name: Optionally automate Gmail forwarding
steps.text: If email receipts still slip through, build a Zapier Zap or a Make scenario that sends labelled Gmail receipts to your QuickBooks forwarding address. Test it with one receipt before you switch it on.

steps.name: Run a 10-minute weekly review
steps.text: Once a week, capture any stray paper receipts and clear the For review list. Then look for bank transactions with no receipt and for duplicates, and note anything you want to ask your accountant about.

sections.heading: How to scan receipts into QuickBooks Online automatically: the three built-in options
paragraphs: QuickBooks Online has three built-in ways to capture receipts: the mobile app camera, a unique forwarding email address, and bulk upload in the Receipts tab. Most businesses use all three, because receipts arrive on paper, by email and in old piles that need clearing.

Mobile app camera: In the QuickBooks mobile app, open the + or New menu and choose the receipt option, which is often called Receipt snap. Photograph the receipt and it goes to the Receipts list in your company file, where QuickBooks reads it. This is the best option for paper receipts, because you can capture them at the till before they fade or get lost. Some versions of the app also let you upload an existing photo from your camera roll.

Email forwarding address: In the Receipts tab on the web, choose the option to forward receipts from email. QuickBooks gives your company a unique address and asks which email addresses are allowed to send to it. Emails from senders not on that list are typically ignored. Copy the address from your own account rather than from a forum post. Intuit's help pages explain how emails with several attachments, or none, are handled.

Bulk upload: On a computer, open the Receipts tab and drag in several files at once, or use the upload button. Depending on your navigation layout, the tab sits under Transactions or Banking. Bulk upload is the fastest way to clear a backlog you've scanned with a phone scanning app or a desk scanner. Save one receipt per file, because a single PDF containing a stack of receipts is likely to be read as one document.
bullets: Lay paper receipts flat on a dark, plain surface so the edges and text stand out.
Keep the vendor name, date and total in the frame. The automatic reading relies on these fields.
Use even light and hold the phone parallel to the paper to avoid glare and shadows.
Capture paper receipts the same day. Thermal paper fades quickly in a wallet or a hot car.
Give your own backup scans consistent names, such as 2026-10-03_VendorName_42.50.pdf, so they sort by date and are easy to search.
Before a bulk upload, check Intuit's help pages for accepted file types and size limits.

sections.heading: What happens after upload: automatic reading and bank matching
paragraphs: After a receipt arrives, QuickBooks reads it and creates a draft transaction. The draft waits in the Receipts tab's For review list until you confirm it. The reading usually fills in the payee (vendor), the date, the total and a suggested category, and you can edit any of these before saving. Depending on your region, it may also pick up sales tax or VAT details, which are worth checking carefully.

Matching is the step that saves the most time. QuickBooks compares the receipt's amount and date with transactions downloaded from your connected bank and card accounts, and suggests a match when it finds a close fit. Confirming the match attaches the receipt image to the existing bank transaction. Your books then show one transaction with its proof attached, rather than two separate entries.

If there is no match yet, usually because the card charge hasn't downloaded, you can either wait or create an expense from the receipt. If you create the expense first, QuickBooks will often suggest matching it when the bank transaction appears in the bank feed later. Accept that suggestion. If you add the bank transaction as a new entry instead, the cost is recorded twice.

Worked example (illustrative figures): on Tuesday you photograph a lunch receipt for 42.50. On Thursday a card charge of 50.00 from the same restaurant downloads, because you added a tip. The amounts differ, so QuickBooks may not suggest a match. Change the receipt amount to 50.00, which is what actually left your account, then match it to the charge. If no suggestion appears, search for the transaction manually.

Suggested categories usually follow how you've categorised that vendor before, plus any bank rules you've set up. Correcting mistakes consistently tends to improve the suggestions. But a wrong category that you accept a few times can become the default, which is another reason to review weekly.
bullets: Match: attaches the receipt to a bank or card transaction that already exists. Use it whenever the charge has downloaded.
Create expense (or bill): records a new transaction from the receipt. Use it for cash purchases or for accounts that aren't connected to QuickBooks.
Edit before you confirm: you can change the payee, date, amount, category and payment account on the review screen.

Newer AI features: Intuit has been adding AI tools, for example under the Intuit Assist name. If your account offers settings that confirm receipts without a review, read exactly what they do before you switch them on.

sections.heading: Settings that help receipts match on the first try
paragraphs: A few one-off settings do more for automatic matching than any capture trick: complete bank feeds, a full list of approved senders and tidy vendor names. Set them up once and the For review list becomes quicker to clear.

Bank feeds matter most, because QuickBooks can only suggest a match for a transaction it has already downloaded. Connect every account you pay business expenses from, including secondary cards. Fix any feed that shows a connection error, because a broken feed stops new matches without warning you.
bullets: Approved senders: list every address that will send to your QuickBooks receipt address. That might include your own inbox, a co-owner's, your bookkeeper's and any shared accounts inbox.

Bank rules: create a rule for each regular vendor so its charges are always categorised the same way. For example, if the bank description contains the vendor's name, assign the category Software. You'll find rules in the bank transactions area of QuickBooks.

Be careful with auto-add: some rules can confirm bank transactions automatically. Test how this works with receipt matching in your account before you rely on it, so receipts don't end up unattached or duplicated.
Vendor names: tidy up duplicate vendors, such as two versions of the same online shop, so category suggestions learn from a single history.
Payment account: set the correct card, bank or cash account on each receipt. This puts the expense in the right place and makes reconciling your accounts easier.

sections.heading: Where the AI reading gets receipts wrong
paragraphs: The automatic reading works best on crisp, printed receipts in a single currency. It is least reliable on faded thermal paper, foreign currency, tipped bills and split purchases, so check these by eye every time.

Faded thermal receipts: Many till receipts are printed on heat-sensitive paper that fades with heat, light and handling. Faint print leads to misread digits, such as a 3 read as an 8, or a missing date. If a receipt is already faint, type in the amount and date from your bank or card statement, and still attach the image as evidence.

Foreign currency: A receipt from abroad may be read in the wrong currency, or with the decimal and thousands separators swapped (1.234,50 versus 1,234.50). Your card statement shows a converted amount, sometimes plus a separate foreign transaction fee, so automatic matching often fails. Match these receipts manually by date and vendor. If you regularly deal in other currencies, read about the QuickBooks multicurrency setting and talk to your accountant before turning it on, because it generally can't be turned off afterwards.

Tips and gratuities: Restaurant and taxi receipts are often printed before the tip is added, so the card charge is higher than the receipt total. The reading may also pick up the subtotal instead of the final total. Treat the bank amount as what you actually paid, and attach the signed tip slip if you have one.

Split purchases: One receipt can cover several categories, mix business and personal items, or be paid partly by card and partly in cash. The reading gives you one total and one category. To divide the amount, use the split option in the bank feed, or on the receipt review screen if your version has one. How to record a personal portion depends on your business structure, so ask your accountant.
bullets: Duplicates: if you capture the same receipt twice, for example by photographing it at the till and later receiving it by email, you get two drafts. Delete one before confirming.
Vendor name mismatches: the receipt may show a trading name while your bank shows a parent company or payment processor, which can confuse matching.
Refunds and returns: a refund receipt may be read as a purchase. Check whether the amount should reduce an expense rather than add a new one.

sections.heading: A 10-minute weekly review routine that stops errors piling up
paragraphs: If your business has a modest number of receipts, ten minutes once a week is often enough to keep matches accurate. A week of receipts is small enough to check quickly and recent enough to remember. Pick a fixed time, such as Monday morning when your bank feeds have had the weekend to update, and make it a recurring calendar event.

If the routine regularly runs past ten minutes, the fix is usually earlier in the process. Capture paper receipts the same day, send more email receipts to the forwarding address automatically, or add bank rules for vendors you pay regularly.
bullets: Minutes 0–2, capture stragglers: empty your wallet, bag and car of paper receipts and photograph them in the app. Check that last week's emailed receipts reached the Receipts tab.
Minutes 2–6, clear the For review list: sort by date, open each suggested match and check the amount, date, payee and category. Fix any misreads, then confirm.
Minutes 6–8, find missing receipts: look in the bank feed for business transactions above an amount you choose that have no receipt attached, and track those receipts down.
Minutes 8–9, catch duplicates: look for the same vendor, amount and date appearing twice in recent transactions, then undo or delete the extra one.

Minutes 9–10, note exceptions: write down anything you weren't sure about, such as a split, a foreign charge or a personal item, to ask your accountant. File or discard paper according to your local record-keeping rules.

sections.heading: Optional: forward Gmail receipts to QuickBooks automatically with Zapier
paragraphs: If most of your receipts arrive in Gmail, a Zapier automation can forward them to your QuickBooks receipt address so you don't have to do it by hand. The setup below uses a Gmail label to start the automation. Zapier renames triggers and actions from time to time, so pick the closest equivalent.

Weigh the trade-offs before you build it. Each forwarded email uses Zapier tasks, and your plan sets task limits and how often Gmail is checked, so confirm current pricing on Zapier's site. Receipts that are only a 'download your invoice' link may give QuickBooks nothing useful to read, so download those PDFs and upload them yourself. You are also giving a third-party service access to your inbox, so keep the search narrow and review the permissions you grant.

There are two alternatives. Gmail's own filters can forward matching emails for free, but Gmail requires you to verify the forwarding address with a confirmation code sent to that address. Check whether this works with your QuickBooks address. Make offers similar Gmail modules in a visual builder and is often cheaper at high volume. Compare current pricing on both sites before you choose.
bullets: Copy your QuickBooks forwarding address from the Receipts tab, and add your Gmail address to its list of approved senders.
In Gmail, create a label such as QBO-receipts and a filter that applies it to your usual receipt senders. Example filter: from:(billing@example.com OR orders@example.net) has:attachment.
In Zapier, create a Zap with Gmail as the trigger app. Choose a trigger such as New Labeled Email, or New Email Matching Search with the search label:qbo-receipts has:attachment.
Add a Gmail Send Email action addressed to your QuickBooks forwarding address, and map the original subject, body and attachment fields.
Send one real receipt through the Zap and check that it appears in the Receipts tab and is read correctly. Only then switch the Zap on.

sections.heading: Check your plan, region and record-keeping rules first
paragraphs: Receipt features differ by QuickBooks Online plan and country version, and rules for digital records differ by tax authority. Confirm both before you rely on scanned copies alone.

Intuit sells different plans in different countries. Features such as receipt capture, multicurrency, bank feed matching and the newer AI tools can vary between plans and change over time. Check the plan comparison and help articles on Intuit's site for your country. Find out what happens to your data and attachments if you downgrade or cancel. Subscription prices also change, so confirm current costs directly with Intuit.

Many tax authorities accept digital copies of receipts if they are legible, complete and can be produced on request. The details vary, though: how long you must keep records, which formats are acceptable, and whether some originals must be kept on paper. Before shredding anything, check your tax authority's guidance (for example the IRS in the US, HMRC in the UK, the CRA in Canada or the ATO in Australia) or ask a qualified accountant. This article is general information, not tax or legal advice.
bullets: Look up your tax authority's rules on digital copies and how long you must keep records.
Consider keeping an independent backup of important receipts, especially for large purchases, so everything isn't stored in one system.

recommendations.best_for: Small businesses, freelancers and bookkeepers who want receipts captured by app, email or bulk upload and matched to bank feeds in the same accounting system.
recommendations.not_for: Teams that need multi-step employee expense approvals or company card programmes, which a dedicated spend-management tool may handle better. It's also not worth leaving accounting software you're happy with just for receipt capture.

recommendations.best_for: People whose receipts mostly arrive in Gmail and who want them forwarded to QuickBooks automatically, with a simple setup that needs no code.
recommendations.not_for: Anyone with very high email volumes on a tight budget, where task costs add up, or anyone uncomfortable giving a third-party service access to their inbox. The built-in forwarding address may be all you need.

recommendations.best_for: Higher-volume or more complex receipt routing, such as several inboxes or filtering by vendor, where a visual builder and a lower cost per run matter. Compare current pricing first.
recommendations.not_for: Beginners who want the quickest setup for a handful of receipts a month. The built-in forwarding address or a simple Zap is usually enough.

faq.question: Does QuickBooks Online read receipts automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. When you upload a receipt through the app, by email or in the Receipts tab, QuickBooks Online reads details such as the vendor, date and amount. It also suggests a category and, where possible, a matching bank transaction. You still review and confirm each receipt, and accuracy drops on faded, foreign-currency or tipped receipts.

faq.question: Where do I find my QuickBooks receipt forwarding email address?
faq.answer: You set it up in the Receipts tab of QuickBooks Online on the web, usually through an option to forward receipts from email. Copy the address from your own account and add the email addresses that are allowed to send to it. If you can't see the option, check Intuit's help pages for your plan and region.

faq.question: Why won't QuickBooks match my receipt to a bank transaction?
faq.answer: The most common reasons are that the charge hasn't downloaded yet, the bank feed has a connection error, the date was misread, or the amounts differ because of a tip, currency conversion or fee. Correct the amount or date on the receipt, then check for a suggestion again or search for the bank transaction manually.

faq.question: Can I throw away paper receipts after scanning them into QuickBooks?
faq.answer: It depends on where you are. Many tax authorities accept clear, complete digital copies, but rules on how long to keep records and in what format vary, and some documents may need to be kept as originals. Check your tax authority's guidance or ask a qualified accountant before you throw paper away.

faq.question: Can I upload multiple receipts to QuickBooks Online at once?
faq.answer: Yes. In the Receipts tab on the web you can drag in or select several files at once. Save one receipt per file for the best results, and check Intuit's help pages for accepted file types and size limits.

faq.question: Do I need Zapier to scan receipts into QuickBooks Online?
faq.answer: No. The mobile app, the forwarding address and bulk upload are all built into QuickBooks Online. Zapier, or a similar tool such as Make, is an optional extra that forwards receipt emails from Gmail automatically, and it adds its own subscription cost.

conclusion: Getting receipts into QuickBooks Online automatically comes down to three habits. Capture each receipt through the right channel on the day it arrives, let QuickBooks read it and suggest the match, and spend ten minutes a week checking its work. Connect your bank feeds first. Choose Match over Create expense whenever the charge already exists, and look closely at faded, foreign-currency, tipped and split receipts. Confirm which features your plan includes on Intuit's site, and check your tax authority's rules before throwing away paper. Add Zapier or Make only if email receipts are still slipping through.
